title: Bhooth Bangla Made ₹264 Crore in Theaters. Tonight, It Arrives on Your Netflix.
excerpt: Akshay Kumar and Priyadarshan's horror-comedy reunion — their first since Bhool Bhulaiyaa — proved the old magic still works. Now the rest of the world gets to find out why.
body:
Here's the thing about **Akshay Kumar** and **Priyadarshan**: when they get together, something chemically different happens. These are the men who gave us **Hera Pheri**. **Garam Masala**. **Bhool Bhulaiyaa**. Films that weren't just hits — they became the shared vocabulary of an entire generation. Dialogue you still quote at family dinners. Characters your uncle does impressions of, badly, after two drinks.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=XW1RkKiRnsg</youtube>

With **Bhooth Bangla**, now streaming on **Netflix** as of today, that partnership has produced another certified blockbuster — ₹264 crore worldwide against a ₹120 crore budget — and for diaspora audiences who missed its theatrical run, this is the weekend sorted.

The premise is classic Priyadarshan: take a completely normal person, drop them into an insane situation, and watch the chaos multiply. Arjun Acharya (Kumar) is a London-based NRI who inherits a crumbling ancestral palace in the fictional village of Mangalpur. Short on cash and long on ambition, he decides to turn the estate into a destination wedding venue for his sister's nuptials. The villagers, naturally, think he's lost his mind.

Because Mangalpur has a problem. A demonic entity called Vadhusur — a bride-hunting spirit straight out of the kind of folklore that keeps you awake in ancestral homes — has been terrorizing the village for generations. Every wedding brings the threat of another bride vanishing. Arjun, being Arjun, ignores all of this. The wedding goes ahead. Things go sideways almost immediately.

What makes Bhooth Bangla work is that it never forgets it's supposed to be fun. The horror elements are atmospheric enough to land — the mansion itself is a production design triumph, all creaking corridors and candlelit shadows — but Priyadarshan keeps the comedy engine running hot. **Rajpal Yadav** is a revelation as a perpetually terrified wedding planner whose survival instinct consists entirely of hiding behind larger people. **Paresh Rawal** delivers exactly the energy you'd expect. And **Tabu** — playing the enigmatic caretaker of the estate — brings a gravity and mystery that anchors the more outlandish sequences.

The Akshay Kumar performance here is worth noting. After a rough patch of films that tested even his most loyal fans' patience, Bhooth Bangla finds him back in his sweet spot: physical comedy, impeccable timing, and the ability to play genuinely scared while making you laugh. There's a sequence involving a possessed dining table and an increasingly panicked Akshay that deserves to be studied in comedy workshops.

**Wamiqa Gabbi**, playing the bride-to-be, brings a feisty warmth that keeps the emotional stakes real even when the film goes deliriously over the top. Her scenes with Kumar have an easy sibling chemistry that grounds the spectacle.

The numbers tell their own story. ₹177 crore India net. ₹54 crore overseas. Over 2.33 lakh theatrical shows across 43 days. On BookMyShow alone, the film sold 33.82 lakh tickets — surpassing the lifetime records of **OMG 2** and **Housefull 5**. It's now Akshay Kumar's third-highest worldwide grosser in the post-pandemic era, behind only **Sooryavanshi** (₹293 crore) and **Housefull 5** (₹288 crore). The producers had already recovered ₹105 crore in non-theatrical deals before the film even opened — ₹60 crore from Netflix alone for digital rights, ₹25 crore from Zee Cinema for satellite, and ₹10 crore from Zee Music.

In other words, this was a profitable film before a single ticket was sold. Everything after that was gravy.

For NRI viewers who've been waiting for the OTT window, Bhooth Bangla is exactly the kind of film that plays beautifully at home. It's a crowd-pleaser — bring the family, crank the volume, and prepare for the uncles to start doing Rajpal Yadav impressions by the interval. The film's references to NRI life — Arjun's London existence, his initial condescension toward the village, his slow reckoning with his roots — add an extra layer for diaspora audiences.

Netflix paid ₹60 crore for the streaming rights. That number alone tells you what the platform thinks of this film's replay value. After seven weeks of theatrical dominance and a worldwide gross that puts it in elite company, Bhooth Bangla arrives on your screen tonight as one of the year's most validated crowd-pleasers.

Bhooth Bangla streams exclusively on Netflix starting today, June 12. Grab the popcorn. Turn the lights off. And maybe keep the biryani away from the dining table — just in case.
